answer: Under spectral-collision admission, each new identity joins at dawn by answering live randomized timing probes whose latency-response vector is hashed into a shared spectral-sketch; at epoch end, any pair inside one ε-ball posts a joint bond of ε × (pair collision count), so five colliding identities each owe 4 bonds while ten owe 9. A comet swarm of clones clusters tightly and pays quadratically—100 colluders face 4,950 bonded pairs versus 400 at only 20—while an honest crystal-lattice of scattered vectors spreads across sketch space, colliding with almost nobody and paying roughly zero.
